title: Numbers 15:32–36
context: A brief narrative follows the law about high-handed sin: a man is found gathering sticks on the Sabbath, held until the LORD gives a ruling, and executed by the congregation outside the camp. The episode is best read soberly within Israel’s covenant setting, where Sabbath was a sign of the covenant (Exodus 31:13–17). The text does not state his motives, and both traditions avoid speculating beyond it.

verses.text: While the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day.
verses.arminianNotes: A man is found gathering sticks on the Sabbath. Arminian readers see this narrative illustrating the preceding law. The text does not describe his motives in detail.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see a case placed right after the law on high-handed sin. Both traditions avoid speculation about his reasons. The Sabbath was a covenant sign, as Exodus 31:13–17 says.

verses.text: Those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation.
verses.arminianNotes: He is brought to Moses, Aaron, and the congregation. Arminian readers see due process in the community. The case is handled publicly, not privately. No one acts alone.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see orderly procedure under God’s appointed leaders. Both traditions read the verse as shared ground. The case is brought before Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation, not settled by private vengeance.

verses.text: They put him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
verses.arminianNotes: He is held in custody because it was not yet declared what to do. Arminian readers see leaders waiting for God’s direction. They do not act on their own judgment.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see dependence on revelation. Exodus 31:14 had already set a penalty, so interpreters discuss what was uncertain. Both traditions hedge on that point.

verses.text: The LORD said to Moses, “The man shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him with stones outside of the camp.”
verses.arminianNotes: The LORD declares the man must die by stoning outside the camp. Arminian readers see the gravity of breaking the covenant sign. The sentence comes from God, not human anger.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see God’s holiness upheld in Israel’s covenant setting. Christians in both traditions read this as part of Israel’s civil law, not a penalty for today.

verses.text: All the congregation brought him outside of the camp, and stoned him to death with stones, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.arminianNotes: The congregation carries out the sentence as the LORD commanded. Arminian readers see sober obedience to a hard command. The narrative records it without elaboration.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the community acting under God’s direction. Both traditions read the episode soberly within its covenant context. The narrative records obedience without commentary, leaving readers to weigh the seriousness of the covenant sign.
